description: ignorePaths: config:recommended pulls in :ignoreModulesAndTests, whose ignorePaths cover **/test/** and **/tests/** -- which silently put the whole tests/ tree out of Renovate's reach. The screenshot harness lives there and carries two real manifests, tests/integration/docker-compose.yml and tests/integration/package.json, so both went unmanaged: the Home Assistant image sat on 2026.5.4 until it fell below the 2026.9.0 floor hacs.json declares and the harness stopped working, and playwright sat on 1.49.1

This is the upstream list with the two test globs dropped and everything else kept. Nothing else under tests/ is a manifest Renovate reads -- the Python tests carry no pins and the rtl_433_tests gitlink is handled by the git-submodules manager, which is disabled by default

customManagers.description: Keep manifest.json requirements in sync with requirements.txt via PyPI
Track Python version in pyproject.toml requires-python

pre-commit.description: Renovate's pre-commit manager is disabled by default, so .pre-commit-config.yaml revs were never updated and drifted behind the equivalent pins in requirements_dev.txt

description: Home Assistant version should match the homeassistant key in hacs.json, so it is not Renovate's to move -- it follows the floor we declare, and the floor is a deliberate support decision rather than a dependency bump

That covers the screenshot harness image as well as the Python pin. The harness must run the *oldest* release we claim to support: on a newer one it would pass while the integration was quietly broken for everyone sitting on the minimum, which is the opposite of what pinning it is for. tests/test_harness_pins.py fails if the image and hacs.json drift apart

packageRules.description: Python version is manually managed to track Home Assistant requirements
prBodyNotes: Do not automerge. This project tracks the Home Assistant Python requirement, which is the previous minor version of Python. Verify the new version matches before merging.

packageRules.description: Group developer tooling updates into a single PR

The test pins live in both requirements_test.txt (CI, pip users) and the pyproject dependency-groups dev group (so a bare `uv run pytest` bootstraps itself). Sharing one group keeps both in a single PR so they cannot drift apart

description: pyrtl_433 needs a group of its own because its pin is repeated five times -- manifest.json (read by both the homeassistant-manifest manager and the custom regex manager), requirements.txt, requirements_test.txt and the pyproject dev dependency-group -- and all five have to move in one commit

It must not share the `test dependencies` group. When a branch mixes a cooldown-blocked upgrade with one that has cleared its cooldown, Renovate drops the blocked upgrade from the branch and does not report it anywhere: not as a PR, and not in the Pending section of the dependency dashboard. pytest-homeassistant-custom-component releases most days, so the shared branch had almost always cleared its cooldown, and every fresh pyrtl_433 release was silently discarded
Both spellings are listed because matchPackageNames resolves against the PyPI-normalized name (pyrtl-433), while the requirements and manifest.json managers report the raw underscore form

packageRules.description: Hook revs are developer tooling. Sharing the group above keeps the ruff== pin in requirements_dev.txt and the ruff-pre-commit rev in one PR, so the two cannot drift apart
Tagged action releases: cooldown, then automerge
Major action bumps: cooldown, then automerge
Pure digest moves: no timestamp available, always review

description: Nothing in CI runs the screenshot harness -- it is a maintainer tool driven by hand from tests/integration/run-harness.sh -- so a green test suite says nothing about whether a new Home Assistant, rtl_433 or Playwright still drives it. The repository automerges by default, which would land those bumps entirely unverified

Bumps here also invalidate committed artifacts rather than just code: the docs/images screenshots are captured through this harness, and Home Assistant's own chrome moves between releases, so a version bump means someone has to re-run the harness and recommit the images
So: open the PR, because knowing a new Home Assistant is out is the point, but never merge it unattended

The Home Assistant image is not in this group's scope: the rule above disables it outright, because it tracks the hacs.json floor rather than the newest release. What is left here is rtl_433, node, playwright and ws

Packages this org publishes carry no cooldown before automerge. minimumReleaseAge exists to leave room for a compromised or yanked third-party release to be pulled before Renovate merges it; on a package we publish ourselves there is nothing to wait to find out

The cooldown also actively hurts here. Releases from our own repositories can land less than three days apart (pyrtl_433 0.3.0 and 0.4.0 were 17 hours apart), and internalChecksFilter is strict, so Renovate holds the newest version rather than falling back to an older one that has aged -- under a fast release cadence the bump stalls indefinitely instead of merely being delayed

Matched on sourceUrl rather than by name so a new first-party dependency is covered the day it is added, and so it holds for every manager: PyPI pins today, an rtl-433-hass action tomorrow. Renovate re-applies packageRules with the sourceUrl in scope before the cooldown is evaluated, so this reaches minimumReleaseAge

Listed last on purpose. packageRules are applied in order and the later rule wins, so this has to sit below the github-actions rules above, which would otherwise put a three day hold back on a first-party action
What stays is the check that actually matters: automerge still waits for the full test suite to pass against the new release
